# GENERATED by scripts/sync-claude.ts — edit scripts/sync-claude.ts instead
description: Implement a feature's UI, verify it in a real browser, screenshot both viewports, checkpoint, then stop for feedback
argument-hint: "<feature|spec-path>"
---

Implement the UI for `$1`, verify it in a real browser, screenshot both viewports, checkpoint the
work, then stop for feedback.

`$1` is either a feature description or the path to a spec file — if it names an existing file,
read that file and use its contents as the spec. Read `./aw.config.json` for `app.frontend`,
`app.baseUrl`, `viewports` and `offLimits`. If `$1` is empty, stop and ask what to build — that
is the only question this command may ask.

PLAYWRIGHT MCP IS REQUIRED for every browser step. Before the first one, check that the
`mcp__playwright__browser_*` tools are available. If they are not, STOP and tell the developer
to run `claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest` and restart Claude Code
(docs/HANDOFF.md Step 1). Never substitute curl, a headless script or a described screenshot
for a real browser check.

1. **Slug.** `<slug>` = the first 6 words of the feature, lowercased and hyphenated
   (≤ 60 chars).
   Every screenshot for this run goes under `screenshots/<slug>/`.
2. **App.** The frontend must be running at `http://localhost:<app.frontend.port>` (or
   `app.baseUrl`). If it is not, start `app.frontend.start` (and `app.backend.start` when
   configured) in the background from the repo root, wait until it answers, and stop whatever you
   started when the run ends. Never leave a server or a watcher behind.
3. **Plan.** Read the backend contract first — the routes, payloads and auth the screens depend
   on — then print a plan of at most 5 short lines (screens, components, states). No preamble,
   no code, no headings.
4. **Implement.** Delegate to the **ui-designer** subagent (Task) with: the plan, the feature or
   spec, the frontend URL, the backend base URL, the repo root, `screenshots/<slug>/`, the
   viewports, and `offLimits`. It edits files with Write/Edit; it never starts or stops a server,
   never runs `git add`/`git commit`/`git push`, and never asks questions — an open product
   decision is resolved the way the existing app resolves it and recorded as a judgment call.
5. **Verify in the browser.** For every touched screen, at BOTH viewports (mobile
   `viewports.mobile`, default 375x812; desktop `viewports.desktop`, default 1440x900):
   `browser_resize` → `browser_navigate` → exercise the interactive states (hover, click, submit,
   loading, error, empty) → `browser_console_messages` must come back clean →
   `browser_take_screenshot` saved as `screenshots/<slug>/<screen>-<viewport>.png` (e.g.
   `screenshots/user-profile-page/settings-mobile.png`). Fix and re-check until console errors
   are gone, both viewports render correctly and the screen matches the rest of the app.
   At least one screenshot per touched screen per viewport is MANDATORY: with no screenshot the
   work counts as unfinished — say so and stop rather than presenting it.
6. **Checkpoint.** `git add -A && git commit -m "design-loop(<slug>): checkpoint"` from the repo
   root. If the tree is clean, skip it and say nothing was committed. **NEVER `git push`**, never
   open or comment on a PR, never amend or rebase — the checkpoint is a local safety net and the
   human decides what leaves the machine.
7. **Present and STOP.** Print three blocks and nothing else after them:
   `CHANGED FILES:` (one per line, from the checkpoint), `SCREENSHOTS:` (every path saved this
   run), `JUDGMENT CALLS:` (one bullet each, or `(none reported)`). Then print this line exactly:

```
--- STOPPING FOR FEEDBACK — resume with: aw design-loop "$1" --iterate "<your feedback>" ---
```

   `$1` is substituted for real: print the feature you were given, so the line can be copied
   and run as it stands.

   Inside this session the developer can also just reply with the feedback. On feedback, apply it
   to the existing implementation and re-run steps 5–7 for the AFFECTED SCREENS ONLY — do not
   rebuild what was already approved, and do not re-screenshot untouched screens.
